svg.title: Robin Hood hashing against linear probing: two tables slot by slot with the terms explained at the slots, probes against load, three results
svg.text: Robin Hood hashing
the same slots, the same average walk to a key; the furthest key 36 slots from home instead of 622
64 or more
1–3 slots away
at home
empty
one cell per slot; colour: how far its key sits from home
A key's hash names its home slot. If that is taken, the key goes into the next free slot, however far: its
displacement. This key came late into a long run of taken slots, a cluster, and sits 622 slots from home.
A key at home: a lookup finds it with one probe,
one slot looked at.
An empty slot ends a search: only here is it known that a
key is not in the table, a miss.
Robin Hood changes one rule: when two keys want a slot, the one further from home gets it and the other moves on. The
same 3,686 keys end up in the same slots, and the distances from home add up to the same 22,789 (checked while
drawing), but the furthest key, this one, is 36 slots out.
Probes per lookup as the table fills
load: the share of slots in use
thick: a miss
thin: the worst hit
black: a hit, the same for both rules (checked)
fewer probes for a miss at load 0.90
shorter worst hit there: 32 probes instead of 390
the time of a hit in plain Python: the price of one more comparison per probe
Where each number comes from
counted by harness.py: exact, the same on every run
timed once, on one machine: logs/bench.txt
